To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the K3 gene product of Kaposi's Sarcoma‐associated Herpesvirus (K3) is a viral E3 ligase that ubiquitinates MHC class I and degrades the receptor.

Kaposi's‐associated herpesviral K3 protein‐mediated lysine‐63 polyubiquitinated MHC class I is targeted for clathrin‐mediated endocytosis, which is dependent on epsin‐dependent endocytic adaptor protein.
lysine‐63 linked polyubiquitinylation by a viral E3 ligase is required for the endocytic degradation of cell surface major histocompatibility complex class I molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of viral immune evasion and how viruses exploit host cell processes for their own replication.
how the immune system detects and responds to infection and how viruses subvert the immune response.
the ubiquitin‐dependent regulation of MHC class I and the role of the K3 ubiquitin E3‐ligase from Kaposi’s sarcoma‐associated Herpes virus in downregulating class I expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lysine‐63 linked polyubiquitinylation of MHC class I by the viral K3 ubiquitin ligase leads to clathrin‐mediated endocytosis of the complex and subsequent degradation by lysosomal proteases.
lysine‐63 linked polyubiquitinated MHC class I is targeted to the endolysosome for degradation by clathrin‐mediated endocytosis, which requires the epsin‐mediated endosomal pathway.
KSHV‐encoded K3 protein targets MHC class I to lysosomes for degradation via a novel ubiquitination‐dependent pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
K3 targets class I to an endocytic pathway that is mediated by lysine‐linked polyubiqutination, which is initiated by a UbcH5‐conjugating enzyme and completed by Ubc13.
the K3 protein of KSHV uses the lysine‐63 ubiquitin chain to target class I for endocytosed degradation.
lysine‐63 ubiquitination is a key signal for endocytotic and endolysomal degradation of MHC class I, which is mediated by the UbcH5‐Ubc13 conjugating enzymes and the epsin adaptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ubiquitination of MHC class I is not sufficient to induce their degradation.
lysine‐63 polyubiquitinated proteins can be internalized by clathrin‐mediated endocytosis.

lysine‐63 polyubiquitinated MHC class I is targeted for endolysosome-mediated degradation, which is mediated by UbcH5 and Ubc13 E2s, as well as the clathrin adaptor epsin, and that monoubiquitin modification is an inefficient internalization signal.
